fact: The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 commits the Government to roll out Electronic Medical Records to all districts, linking PHUs and referral hospitals, phased from high-volume districts; its action plan sets a costed strategy for the phased roll-out by 2027 and roll-out to all medical facilities by 2030.

The Compact's action plan names the Ministry of Health's Directorate of Policy Planning and Information (DPPI) as lead institution for both the costed EMR roll-out strategy (2027) and the roll-out of EMR to all medical facilities (2030).

The Roadmap's table of digital health tools, from the Ministry's landscape assessment of 15-29 November 2022, lists DHIS2 as the Health Management Information System, deployed by the MoH in all districts and at the 'scaled' stage.

The National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026, the Ministry's guiding document for three years, carries a section on the District Health Management Information System (3.5.1) under Services and Applications, which takes NLe 142.5 million (US$6.07 million, 63.6%) of an indicative US$10.0 million costing; the section's text is outside the capture. The document gives the span 2024-2026 and no publication day.

The Roadmap states that the digital health interventions assessed in November 2022, DHIS2 among them, were 83% donor driven and 17% private sector funded with no significant public contribution, that only 1% of the US$1.2 million needed for the 2018 strategy was budgeted by the MoH in 2019 and half of that released, and that the MoH's 2022 statutory budget had no provision for digital health. The figure covers all interventions, not DHIS2 alone.
